general_background.title: Cadmium oxide needs conversion to a soluble feed
general_background.summary: Cadmium oxide is a solid precursor that can be converted into a soluble cadmium complex by an acidic ligand. That conversion makes it possible to control the cadmium delivered during nucleation without using a volatile organocadmium feed.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Formation of High-Quality CdTe, CdSe, and CdS Nanocrystals Using CdO as Precursor

general_background.title: Technical-grade TOPO is not always chemically equivalent to purified TOPO
general_background.summary: Phosphorus-containing impurities in technical-grade TOPO can change cadmium precursor coordination and surface binding during colloidal growth. They can therefore change shape selection without a change in the nominal solvent name.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: The Trouble with TOPO; Identification of Adventitious Impurities Beneficial to the Growth of Cadmium Selenide Quantum Dots, Rods, and Wires

general_background.title: TOPO as a coordinating medium
general_background.summary: Trioctylphosphine oxide supplies a coordinating medium in which metal chalcogenide nanocrystals can nucleate and grow. Coordination at the particle surface influences which growth sites remain accessible and how the particles disperse afterward.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Stable cluster intermediates can delay particle growth
general_background.summary: In some indium phosphide routes, unusually stable molecular clusters accumulate instead of turning immediately into a smoothly growing distribution. Their appearance breaks the simple link between mixing the precursor and forming the final nanocrystals.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
